details:
Project Details – ECHOES: THE LAST SIGNAL

ECHOES: THE LAST SIGNAL is an interactive 3D space archive that explores what happens to spacecraft and scientific equipment after their missions come to an end. It brings the stories of three remarkable NASA missions to life: the Apollo 11 Lunar Module, the Opportunity Mars Rover, and the Dawn spacecraft.

What does it do and how does it work?

Visitors enter an interactive space environment where they can select and explore the three missions. Each mission features a 3D spacecraft model that users can rotate, zoom into, and examine. An interactive component explorer explains important spacecraft systems and their purpose. Mission histories, timelines, discoveries, and information about equipment left behind provide context. Dedicated audio briefings and discovery narrations make the experience more engaging.

The application brings together NASA resources, 3D visualization, interactive exploration, and storytelling to create an engaging learning experience.

What benefits does it have?

The project makes space exploration more accessible and interesting for students, educators, and anyone curious about science and technology. Rather than relying only on static images and text, visitors can interact with spacecraft models and understand the engineering behind their missions. It also highlights an often-overlooked part of space exploration: the machines that remain on other worlds after their missions are complete.

What is the intended impact?

The aim is to encourage curiosity about space science, spacecraft engineering, and the legacy of human exploration. I want visitors to understand that the end of a mission does not mean the end of its story. These machines represent years of research, engineering, problem-solving, and human ambition. By presenting their stories in an interactive format, ECHOES aims to make these achievements more memorable and inspire interest in science, technology, engineering, and space exploration.

What tools and technologies were used?

I independently conceptualized, designed, coded, and developed the project using:

  • Languages: JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS.
  • Frontend: React and Vite.
  • 3D development: Three.js and React Three Fiber.
  • Backend: Supabase for database integration, anonymous user sessions, and mission progress tracking.
  • Development environment: Visual Studio Code.
  • Deployment: Netlify.
  • Audio: Google AI Studio for narration generation and audio integration.

I used AI-assisted tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Bolt.new selectively throughout development. They helped me explore implementation approaches, troubleshoot coding issues, refine the project structure, improve the storytelling, and develop narration. I reviewed, adapted, integrated, and tested the code and features as I built the application.

How is the project creative?

The central creative idea is to tell the stories of spacecraft from the perspective of what remains after a mission ends. Instead of presenting conventional mission summaries, the project treats each spacecraft as an explorer with its own journey and legacy.

The three featured missions offer very different stories: Apollo 11 represents humanity's first crewed lunar landing, Opportunity represents extraordinary endurance on Mars, and Dawn represents the exploration of two distinct worlds. Their stories come together through interactive 3D models, component exploration, dedicated environments, and audio storytelling.

What factors were considered during development?

As a solo developer, I considered the following factors while building the experience:

  • Scientific accuracy: Using NASA resources for mission information and spacecraft references.
  • Educational value: Making spacecraft components and mission achievements understandable to a broad audience.
  • User experience: Keeping navigation simple and allowing visitors to explore at their own pace.
  • Visual engagement: Giving each mission its own environment and interactive 3D experience.
  • Performance: Keeping 3D models and audio suitable for a browser-based application.
  • Accessibility: Providing both written information and audio narration.
  • Technical feasibility: Using web technologies so visitors can access the project through a standard browser without specialized software.

ECHOES: THE LAST SIGNAL is my effort to bring attention to the stories behind these remarkable machines and remind people that every silent spacecraft has a legacy worth discovering.
